content.text:
Here are the **best laptop-deal leads I found online today, June 7, 2026**. Since prices/stock can change quickly, treat these as “check first” deals rather than guaranteed checkout prices.

## Best current deal leads

| Best for | Deal / place to check | Why it’s worth a look |
|---|---|---|
| **Budget Chromebook** | **Best Buy Chromebook deals starting around $219** | Good if you mainly browse, stream, use Google Docs, email, and school apps. TechRadar noted Best Buy had several Chromebook deals starting at $219 this week. ([techradar.com](https://www.techradar.com/computing/deals?utm_source=openai)) |
| **Mainstream Windows laptop under ~$500** | **Lenovo IdeaPad / Slim-series deals at Best Buy or Lenovo** | Recent deal coverage flagged Lenovo Ryzen 7 / 16GB RAM / 512GB SSD configurations around the low-$400 range at Best Buy. Look for **16GB RAM + 512GB SSD** minimum if possible. ([techradar.com](https://www.techradar.com/pro/lenovo-ryzen-7-laptop-with-16gb-ram-and-512gb-ssd-is-just-usd430-at-best-buy-but-it-wont-be-this-price-for-long?utm_source=openai)) |
| **Student / thin-and-light Windows laptop** | **Dell XPS 13 — starting $699, student deal $599** | Dell’s new XPS 13 is positioned as a lower-cost premium ultraportable, with a reported **$599 student deal** for back-to-school. Good if you want portability and build quality. ([tomshardware.com](https://www.tomshardware.com/laptops/dell-xps-13-targets-macbook-neo-with-intels-wildcat-lake-usd699-starting-price-usd599-for-students?utm_source=openai)) |
| **MacBook deal** | **Best Buy Apple sale — MacBooks included, up to $400 off Apple tech** | If you want macOS, Best Buy is currently a strong place to check because it’s running a limited-time Apple sale including MacBooks. ([techradar.com](https://www.techradar.com/seasonal-sales/best-buy-slashes-up-to-usd400-off-apple-tech-in-its-limited-time-sale-get-airpods-macbooks-ipads-and-apple-watches-from-usd99-99?utm_source=openai)) |
| **Gaming laptop value** | **Lenovo Legion 5i RTX 5060 at B&H / deal trackers** | TechRadar highlighted a Lenovo Legion 5i deal with **RTX 5060, OLED display, Core Ultra 7, 32GB RAM, and $400 off** as one of the best gaming-laptop deals it had seen that week. ([techradar.com](https://www.techradar.com/computing/deals?utm_source=openai)) |
| **Dell / Alienware gaming laptop** | **Dell Alienware deals page** | Tom’s Hardware is tracking Dell/Alienware deals, including Alienware 16 Aurora configurations with RTX 50-series graphics. Good if you want gaming performance and prefer buying direct from Dell. ([tomshardware.com](https://www.tomshardware.com/news/dell-alienware-deals?utm_source=openai)) |
| **General deal hunting** | **Tom’s Hardware laptop deals page** | Tom’s Hardware says it continuously updates notebook deals across Amazon, Dell, Lenovo, and others, so it’s a good hub to compare current offers. ([tomshardware.com](https://www.tomshardware.com/desktops/best-laptop-pc-deals-productivity?utm_source=openai)) |

## My quick picks by budget

- **Under $250:** Chromebook from Best Buy — fine for light use, not ideal for gaming or heavy multitasking.
- **$350–$500:** Lenovo IdeaPad/Slim, HP Pavilion, or Asus VivoBook with **16GB RAM + 512GB SSD**.
- **$600–$800:** Dell XPS 13 student deal, MacBook sale models, or a nicer Lenovo Yoga/IdeaPad Pro.
- **$900–$1,300:** Gaming laptop with **RTX 5060/5070**, 16–32GB RAM, and 1TB SSD if possible.
- **$1,300+:** Premium MacBook, Lenovo Legion, Asus ROG/Zephyrus, Dell XPS, or Alienware—only worth it if you need performance, display quality, or build quality.

## What to look for before buying

For most people, I’d avoid any Windows laptop with **only 8GB RAM** unless it’s very cheap. Aim for:

- **RAM:** 16GB minimum; 32GB for gaming, creative work, coding, or heavy multitasking.
- **Storage:** 512GB SSD minimum; 1TB if gaming or media-heavy.
- **CPU:** Recent Intel Core Ultra, AMD Ryzen 5/7, Apple M-series, or Snapdragon X-series.
- **Display:** 1080p minimum; OLED is a bonus if priced well.
- **Return policy:** Buy from Best Buy, Amazon, Costco, Dell, Lenovo, B&H, or another reputable seller.

If you tell me your **budget**, **preferred size**, and whether it’s for **school, work, gaming, or travel**, I can narrow this to 3–5 specific models to buy.
